picks.intervention_label: Datopotamab deruxtecan +/- durvalumab on TROPION-Breast05 (NCT06103864)
picks.rationale: This is the trial the patient's preference set was written for. Actively recruiting, 1L, biomarker-gated on the pending CPS result, randomized against the same KEYNOTE-355 backbone we would give her off-trial. Trial-first preference satisfied, no toxicity vetoes triggered, TROP2-ADC mechanism hits the basal-feature axis. If she draws the control arm she gets standard-of-care anyway, so the downside is bounded.
primary_concerns: Gated on pending PD-L1 CPS by 22C3 >=10; if CPS <10 the patient is not eligible for this trial and the rank collapses.
Trial-first preference fully satisfied; efficacy lean (0.7) honored by the experimental TROP2-ADC + ICI arm; no toxicity vetoes to violate.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin/gemcitabine (KEYNOTE-355 1L backbone)
picks.rationale: Standard 1L backbone if PD-L1 CPS returns >=10. The carboplatin/gemcitabine flavor of the regimen pulls double duty against BRCA1-mutated disease, which sweetens the choice for this patient. Efficacy weight 0.7 with no vetoes makes the triplet acceptable, and the TIL-3+/TMB-14 phenotype is the subset that retrospectively benefits most in KEYNOTE-522 and KEYNOTE-355 analyses. If CPS comes back under 10, this pick falls off the list and Dato-DXd on TROPION-Breast02 takes its place.
primary_concerns: Same CPS-gating dependency as pick 1.
Off-trial standard of care; trial preference partially honored only by virtue of being TROPION-Breast05's control arm.
Efficacy/toxicity preference satisfied: KEYNOTE-355 HR 0.65 PFS and HR 0.73 OS in CPS>=10 is the efficacy-leaning choice she would consent to at 0.7.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID (BRCA1-directed PARPi, OlympiAD label)
picks.rationale: Oral, single-agent, and if the germline BRCA1 test confirms, the FDA label is right there. Between OlympiAD (olaparib) and EMBRACA (talazoparib) the efficacy is close; talazoparib has the harder hematologic profile. With efficacy weight 0.7 and no anemia veto, either is defensible. I would advocate for olaparib first because the tolerability margin lets her stay on therapy longer and combines more easily with later liver-directed local consolidation.
primary_concerns: Eligibility gated on germline BRCA1 resolution; somatic-only BRCA1 takes her off the OlympiAD/EMBRACA label and onto the somatic-BRCA Stanford trial (NCT03990896) instead.
Modality (oral) is not constrained by the preferences file but is a defensible advocate-tilt toward lower-footprint therapy for a 42-year-old with a curative-intent framing.
Single-agent PARPi in 1L mTNBC is less aggressive than ICI + chemo; honors efficacy lean but does not maximize it. Suitable as a bridge or for the post-induction maintenance question.

picks.intervention_label: SBRT to solitary liver lesion as consolidation on MSK SABR-COMET-style trial (NCT05534438) after systemic response
picks.rationale: The preferences file is explicit about the curative-intent framing, and a solitary 1.5 cm hepatic lesion is the most consolidatable disease pattern this patient will ever have. The NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS readout was negative, which tempers the case honestly. The MSK trial enrolls specifically de novo oligometastatic disease (not mixed with oligoprogression) and lets her get SBRT under protocol once systemic response is documented. I would advocate enrolling after a 12-week response assessment confirms control of the breast and axillary primary.
primary_concerns: NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS readout was negative for the consolidation arm; the curative-intent rationale rests on biology selection rather than a positive randomized signal.
Layered on top of (not instead of) the systemic regimen from picks 1-3; honors the free-text curative framing without abandoning systemic backbone.
Trial-first preference satisfied via the MSK protocol slot; modality preference is silent.

picks.intervention_label: ZEN-3694 (BET inhibitor) + pembrolizumab + nab-paclitaxel (phase 1b, NCT05422794)
picks.rationale: Closest active trial to the patient's MYC-amp + basal + TIL-rich + ICI-favorable axis, with all four pieces aligned. Phase 1b means small numbers and a real cumulative toxicity signal layering BET-i on pembrolizumab + nab-paclitaxel. Efficacy weight 0.7, no vetoes, and the stated trial preference make this fit the slot her profile was set up for. I rank it 5 because TROPION-Breast05's control arm already covers most of the ICI + chemo bet without the BET-i overhead.
primary_concerns: Phase 1b dose-finding; efficacy data are early and the toxicity stack of BET-i + pembro + nab-paclitaxel is real, but no toxicity veto is set so this is not blocked on preferences.
Trial-first preference fully satisfied; MYC-amp axis maximally honored.
Geographic accessibility: NCI sites only; if the patient is not near an NCI center this pick demotes on logistics grounds the preferences file does not capture.

notes: Rank order reflects a strict reading of the preference file: trial-first preference (pushes TROPION-Breast05 up), efficacy lean 0.7 (favors ICI+chemo or ADC backbones over single-agent PARPi for 1L), no toxicity vetoes (no eliminated regimens), no modality constraints (oral PARPi is an advocate-tilt rather than a preference-mandated pick). The free-text curative-intent framing is what brings SBRT consolidation onto the list at rank 4; without that note SBRT would not make a 1L systemic-therapy ranking. Picks 1 and 2 are CPS-gated and shift if 22C3 returns <10 (TROPION-Breast02 and TroFuse-011 would replace them). Olaparib at rank 3 is germline-gated; if BRCA1 resolves to somatic-only, the Stanford talazoparib trial (NCT03990896) is the on-trial substitute.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + carboplatin AUC2 / gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (KEYNOTE-355 backbone)
picks.rationale: Contingent on PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3 pharmDx, this is the 1L regimen with the deepest safety dossier for the slot. KEYNOTE-355 reported PFS HR 0.65 (CI 0.49-0.86) and OS HR 0.73 in the CPS>=10 stratum, and pembrolizumab now carries roughly six years of post-approval irAE follow-up plus a codified NCCN/ASCO/SITC toxicity-management algorithm. The carboplatin/gemcitabine flavor doubles as BRCA1-directed cytotoxicity and avoids the cumulative neuropathy that weekly taxane backbones load onto a 42-year-old who may be on therapy for years. If CPS returns <10 this pick collapses and pick 3 takes its place.
primary_concerns: Eligibility is gated on PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3; CPS is pending and discordance between breast primary and liver M1 runs 20-30%.

ICI-related hypothyroidism (~15% any-grade), pneumonitis (G>=3 ~2%), and colitis are the AE classes that demand active surveillance; the management pathway is mature but the patient needs explicit counseling on autoimmune sequelae before consent.
Carboplatin/gemcitabine G>=3 neutropenia ~30-40%; manageable with G-CSF per ASCO 2015 guidance, but adds infection risk that should be discussed up front.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID (OlympiAD, BRCA1-directed PARP inhibitor)
picks.rationale: If the germline BRCA1 test confirms (and the NCCN genetic-familial breast guideline mandates it under 50 anyway), olaparib has nine years of post-approval safety data in this exact indication. OlympiAD G>=3 TRAE 36.6% (versus 50.5% chemo arm), G>=3 anemia 16.1%, discontinuation 4.9% — the cleanest tolerability profile of any single agent on the table. I prefer olaparib over talazoparib here because the EMBRACA G>=3 anemia rate is 39% versus 16.1% for olaparib, and the talazoparib hematologic burden meaningfully compresses dose intensity over a 12-18 month treatment horizon. Use as the 1L choice if she declines or cannot tolerate the KEYNOTE-355 backbone, or as bridging while CPS resolves.
primary_concerns: Gated on germline BRCA1 resolution; somatic-only BRCA1 takes the patient off the OlympiAD/EMBRACA US label and onto off-label or trial pathways.
MDS/AML risk with cumulative PARP-i exposure runs 1-2% across the registrational dataset; the management algorithm requires baseline CBC and serial monitoring, which is established but not zero.
Single-agent PARP-i in 1L M1 TNBC is less aggressive than ICI+chemo on efficacy — appropriate when tolerability is the binding constraint or when CPS<10 closes the pembrolizumab door.

picks.intervention_label: Carboplatin AUC2 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (PD-L1-agnostic 1L backbone in BRCA1-mut TNBC)
picks.rationale: If CPS returns <10 and pick 1 falls away, this is the chemotherapy backbone with the longest safety record in the disease and the strongest mechanistic fit to BRCA1. The TNT signal (HR 0.59 PFS in BRCA-mut subset for carboplatin vs docetaxel) and decades of carboplatin/gemcitabine experience put the AE distribution at well-characterized G>=3 neutropenia 30-40%, thrombocytopenia ~15%, with standard supportive-care algorithms. Cleaner than a taxane platform on neuropathy in a young patient with curative-intent framing.
primary_concerns: Cytopenias are the binding toxicity; weekly CBC monitoring and G-CSF/transfusion thresholds need to be set up front.
Cumulative platinum nephrotoxicity is rare with carboplatin but warrants baseline creatinine clearance documentation.

No randomized first-line OS data for carboplatin/gemcitabine specifically in PD-L1-low BRCA1-mut mTNBC; the regimen rests on TNT-derived class evidence plus extensive post-marketing experience rather than a single registrational trial.

picks.intervention_label: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV d1,8 q21d — held in reserve for 2L per ASCENT label
picks.rationale: Not enrollable now (1L treatment-naive), but worth naming on the rank list so the team locks the 2L pivot before she progresses. ASCENT final mOS 11.8 vs 6.9 mo (HR 0.51), five years of post-approval data, and a defined AE profile: G>=3 neutropenia 51%, G>=3 diarrhea 10%, febrile neutropenia 6%, treatment-related death rate 0.4%. The neutropenia signal is large and the SG label now carries a G-CSF primary-prophylaxis recommendation, which makes the toxicity predictable rather than novel. I rank it here so the conservative posture survives intact through the next line.
primary_concerns: Not enrollable in 1L; this is a planning pick, not an active recommendation.

G>=3 neutropenia 51% is the rate-limiting AE and requires G-CSF primary prophylaxis plus active diarrhea management (loperamide algorithm); the supportive-care infrastructure has to be in place before cycle 1.
UGT1A1*28 homozygotes have higher febrile-neutropenia risk; genotype check is recommended though not mandated.

notes: Posture: I'm pushing the order toward regimens with extensive post-marketing safety data and codified AE-management pathways. KEYNOTE-355 is rank 1 because the patient's TIL-3+/TMB-14 phenotype reinforces the ICI rationale on top of an already strong CPS-anchored label, and the carboplatin/gemcitabine flavor pulls double duty on BRCA1. Olaparib at rank 2 because OlympiAD has a meaningfully cleaner G>=3 toxicity distribution than EMBRACA talazoparib (G>=3 anemia 16.1% vs 39%); the talazoparib edge in PFS does not outweigh that delta when the patient is on therapy for the long haul. Carboplatin/gemcitabine at rank 3 is the CPS<10 fallback. SG at rank 4 is forward-planning for 2L. Deliberately omitted: CAPItello-290 (negative OS overall AND in the PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered stratum that would have been her best subgroup); EPIK-B3 (terminated, missed primary); ZEN-3694 phase 1b (BET inhibitor toxicity is uncharacterized in this combination and the trial is dose-finding — does not meet the conservative bar for a 1L pick); SBRT consolidation (NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS readout was negative; SABR-COMET 4.5% treatment-related death rate); inavolisib + eribulin trial (not yet recruiting, TNBC efficacy data zero). Reserving veto power for round 2 if a co-persona surfaces capivasertib in TNBC or BET-i layered on ICI + chemo without compensating safety mitigation.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID (OlympiAD)
picks.rationale: Two independent registrational phase 3 trials anchor PARP inhibition in germline BRCA1/2 HER2-neg mBC: OlympiAD (n=302, PFS HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.43-0.80) and EMBRACA (n=431, PFS HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41-0.71). Both pre-registered, both low RoB 2 across allocation, blinding of outcome assessors (BICR-adjudicated PFS), and selective-reporting domains, both replicated the synthetic-lethality preclinical anchor (Bryant 2005, Farmer 2005). This is the strongest evidence package in the dossier for this patient. The gating step is germline-vs-somatic resolution; the FDA breast label is germline-restricted and the somatic-talazoparib alternative (NCT03990896) is a single-arm n=13 interim ORR readout I would not equate with phase 3 evidence.
primary_concerns: RoB 2 — deviations from intended interventions: both trials open-label. Acceptable because the primary PFS endpoint is BICR-adjudicated, but worth naming.

Germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 unresolved on tumor NGS; somatic-only collapses olaparib to off-label in breast. The Stanford somatic-talazoparib trial (NCT03990896) is n=13 interim, single-arm, ORR-only — not a phase 3 substitute.
Cumulative MDS/AML risk on PARP inhibitor exposure runs 1-2% across the pooled registrational dataset; baseline and serial CBC monitoring is mandated.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab + carboplatin/gemcitabine (KEYNOTE-355) if PD-L1 CPS >=10
picks.rationale: Phase 3 n=847, pre-specified primary PFS endpoint hit in the CPS>=10 stratum at HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.49-0.86, p=0.0012) and OS HR 0.73 at the final readout. RoB 2 low across all domains. The label is biomarker-gated and the CPS<10 subset showed no benefit — the indication tracks the data, not the other way around. Eligibility hinges entirely on the pending 22C3 CPS. PD-L1 discordance between primary and liver M1 in 20-30% of paired samples is a documented confound; the breast block is the right substrate per the 22C3 companion-diagnostic instructions.
primary_concerns: Eligibility entirely gated on PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3 pharmDx; CPS is pending (target_validation row pd-l1-cps-confirmation). CPS <10 closes this regimen, and the patient does NOT inherit the benefit from TMB-14 or 3+ TILs. KEYNOTE-355 was not powered on TMB or TILs; substituting them is unsanctioned biomarker extrapolation.

KEYNOTE-158 TMB-H basket (n=102, single-arm, ORR 29%) is sometimes invoked to bridge the CPS<10 gap. It cannot — the label restricts to >=2L after progression with no satisfactory alternatives, and the absence of a comparator makes the 29% ORR uninterpretable in 1L treatment-naive disease.

RoB 2 risk-of-bias judgment: low across allocation, blinding, missing data, measurement, and selective-reporting domains. Sponsor-conducted analysis flagged but not de-rated; replication via KEYNOTE-522 (early-stage TNBC, different setting) is consistent on direction of effect.

picks.intervention_label: Talazoparib 1 mg PO daily (EMBRACA)
picks.rationale: Second independent phase 3 anchor in the same indication; n=431, PFS HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.71), p<0.001, low RoB 2. Two trials, two sponsors, two molecules, one gating biomarker, replicated direction and magnitude of effect — this is exactly the replication standard the persona is set up to credit. Ranks below olaparib only on tolerability: G>=3 anemia 39% on talazoparib versus 16.1% on olaparib in their respective registrational datasets. Evidence quality is at parity with pick 1.
primary_concerns: Same germline gating as pick 1.
G>=3 anemia 39% materially compresses dose intensity over a 12-18 month treatment horizon, which is a tolerability not an evidence-quality concern.
Same open-label RoB 2 caveat as OlympiAD; BICR-adjudicated PFS is the mitigation.

picks.intervention_label: Carboplatin AUC2 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (PD-L1-low BRCA1-mut fallback)
picks.rationale: If CPS returns <10 and pembrolizumab closes, the BRCA1-directed platinum doublet is the defensible PD-L1-agnostic backbone. The evidence pyramid here is thinner than picks 1-3 and I want to be straight about it: TNT (Tutt 2018, n=376) hit no overall PFS difference between carboplatin and docetaxel, but the pre-specified BRCA-mutated subgroup (n=43) showed PFS HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.36-0.97, p=0.04) favoring carboplatin. n=43 is a small subgroup with a wide CI; this is class evidence plus three decades of carboplatin/gemcitabine post-marketing experience, not a registrational 1L anchor. I rank it 4 because in the CPS<10 contingency it is the least-bad supported option.
primary_concerns: TNT BRCA-mut subgroup is pre-specified but n=43; the HR 0.59 should be cited with its wide CI, not as a primary-endpoint signal.
No registrational 1L OS data for carboplatin/gemcitabine specifically in PD-L1-low BRCA1-mut mTNBC; the regimen rests on TNT class evidence plus post-marketing experience.
G>=3 neutropenia 30-40% and thrombocytopenia ~15% are well-characterized with standard supportive-care algorithms.

notes: Posture: I am ranking on evidence quality (registered primary endpoint hit, replication, RoB 2 grade), not on biological enthusiasm. Picks 1-3 are all phase 3, low RoB, with replicated effects (olaparib/talazoparib mutually replicate; pembrolizumab in mTNBC replicates direction of effect across KEYNOTE-355 and KEYNOTE-522 even though the populations differ). Pick 4 is openly demoted to a contingency slot because TNT's BRCA-mut readout is a small pre-specified subgroup, not a primary-endpoint hit. Vetoes I will raise in round 2 if surfaced: (1) CAPItello-290 capivasertib + paclitaxel in TNBC — phase 3 primary OS NOT MET overall AND in the pre-specified AKT-pathway-altered stratum; basing off-label use in TNBC on that subgroup is the canonical post-hoc reanalysis trap. (2) ZEN-3694 + pembro + nab-paclitaxel (NCT05422794) — n=60 phase 1b dose-finding with no published efficacy and a MYC-amp expansion that is hypothesis-generating, not powered. (3) Inavolisib + eribulin in TNBC (NCT07441512) — n=40 single-arm phase 2, not yet recruiting, off-label in TNBC, gated on a PIK3CA hotspot that is currently ngs_pending; the biomarker gating step is unmet. (4) TOPACIO niraparib + pembrolizumab — single-arm n=55, the BRCA-mut 47% ORR is a post-hoc subset of roughly 14 patients with no comparator. (5) MEDIOLA breast cohort — single-arm n=34, DCR/ORR surrogate, no comparator. (6) Routine off-trial SBRT consolidation of the solitary liver lesion — NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS was negative with HR ~1.31 favoring the systemic-only arm; a randomized signal against the consolidation arm is exactly the data this persona credits. Enrollment on a registered consolidation trial (NCT05534438) is a different question and not vetoed. Two additional notes: (a) the TIL '3+' grade is at risk of being a non-ITWG ad-hoc score — the target_validation row stromal-tils-rescore-itwg flags it as a documentation/re-scoring step before any TIL-anchored argument is leaned on; (b) the TMB 14 mut/Mb value should be locked to an FDA-cleared panel (F1CDx) before it is used to gate anything, per target_validation tmb-panel-assay-confirmation.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg PO BID (OlympiAD label; talazoparib 1 mg daily per EMBRACA is the interchangeable alternative)
picks.rationale: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 lists olaparib and talazoparib as category 1 preferred 1L systemic therapy for HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with a germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant, and the guideline language is explicit that PARP-i can be initiated without waiting for PD-L1 testing once germline BRCA is confirmed. ESMO Clinical Practice Guideline for metastatic breast cancer (Gennari 2021, Ann Oncol; ESMO Living Guidelines refresh 2024) gives PARP-i monotherapy in this indication an MCBS v1.1 score of 4 with evidence level [I, A]. ASCO concurs through its 2020/2024 systemic-therapy guidance. This is the cleanest cross-society convergence point in the dossier for this exact patient.
primary_concerns: Germline-vs-somatic BRCA1 unresolved; the FDA/NCCN breast indication is germline-restricted. If the tumor NGS call is somatic only, the patient sits outside the OlympiAD/EMBRACA label population and PARP-i becomes an off-label call (defensible mechanistically but no longer category 1).
Patient is ECOG 1, which is squarely inside the OlympiAD/EMBRACA enrolled population.
MDS/AML risk on cumulative PARP-i exposure runs 1-2% across the pooled registrational dataset; baseline CBC and serial monitoring are mandated by the labels.

picks.intervention_label: Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg d1,8 q21d + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w (ASCENT-04 / KEYNOTE-D19) — contingent on PD-L1 CPS >=10
picks.rationale: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 (Feb 27 2026 update) elevated sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab to category 1 preferred 1L for metastatic TNBC with PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3, based on ASCENT-04/KEYNOTE-D19 (n=443, PFS 11.2 vs 7.8 mo, HR 0.65, 95% CI 0.51-0.84). The trial included BRCA-mutated patients, so this is a legitimate alternative to PARP-i for the CPS>=10 BRCA1+ subset rather than a competing indication. I rank it second because NCCN positions germline-BRCA-directed PARP-i ahead of CPS-anchored regimens within the same patient when both apply.
primary_concerns: Gated on the pending PD-L1 CPS by 22C3; the patient sits at the gate, not yet inside the guideline-endorsed population.
Guideline elevation is fresh (Feb 2026) and ESMO has not yet published an MCBS score; cross-society convergence is still consolidating around this regimen.
Overall survival was immature at the primary PFS readout — the category 1 designation rests on PFS plus quality-of-life data, not OS.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w + carboplatin AUC2 / gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (KEYNOTE-355) — contingent on CPS >=10
picks.rationale: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 retains KEYNOTE-355 pembrolizumab + chemotherapy as a category 1 preferred 1L regimen for CPS >=10 metastatic TNBC; ESMO Living Guidelines list it with MCBS v1.1 score 4 [I, A]. The carboplatin/gemcitabine flavor doubles as BRCA1-directed cytotoxicity (TNT class evidence), so for this patient it is the next-best CPS-anchored backbone if sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab is not accessible. ASCO Insights and the SGO-endorsed Breast Cancer Committee update both back this position.
primary_concerns: Same CPS-gating as pick 2; the patient is not yet inside the guideline-endorsed population.
After the Feb 2026 NCCN update, SG + pembrolizumab is the preferred CPS >=10 regimen and KEYNOTE-355 chemo+pembro drops to the alternative slot; the rank order here reflects that.
Patient ECOG 1 and treatment-naive — squarely inside the KEYNOTE-355 enrolled population.

picks.intervention_label: Carboplatin AUC2 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m^2 d1,8 q21d (PD-L1-low BRCA1-mut fallback)
picks.rationale: NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 lists single-agent platinum and platinum doublets among preferred 1L chemotherapy options for metastatic TNBC (category 2A); the BRCA1-mut subgroup of the TNT trial (n=43) is the indication-specific evidence with ORR 68% vs 33% and PFS 6.8 vs 4.8 mo favoring carboplatin over docetaxel. ESMO ABC guidance endorses platinum preference in BRCA-mut TNBC in the same language. This is the contingency pick if CPS returns <10, PARP-i is declined or unavailable, and an off-trial chemotherapy backbone is needed.
primary_concerns: The TNT BRCA-mut readout is a pre-specified subgroup at n=43, which is why this sits at NCCN category 2A and not category 1; the guideline endorsement leans on class evidence plus three decades of post-marketing experience.
If germline BRCA1 confirms and PARP-i is offered, this regimen drops below pick 1 in the consensus order.
ECOG 1 patient with normal organ function as far as we know — inside the standard chemotherapy enrolled population.

picks.intervention_label: Defer routine early local therapy of the primary or the solitary liver lesion (per E2108 / NRG-BR002)
picks.rationale: This is a recommendation against, not for, an intervention, and it is exactly the kind of call the concensusite seat is supposed to make. E2108 (ECOG-ACRIN, n=390 randomized post-induction, JCO 2022) showed no OS benefit for early local therapy of the primary in de novo stage IV breast cancer (HR 1.09, 90% CI 0.80-1.49) and worse health-related QoL at 18 months. NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS readout was likewise negative for SBRT/resection consolidation. NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 and ESMO ABC guidance therefore do not endorse routine early surgical or radiation consolidation in de novo M1 disease outside a trial. If the team wants to pursue ablation of the solitary liver lesion, the consensus-aligned route is enrollment on a registered consolidation protocol (e.g. NCT05534438 at MSK) after a documented systemic response — not off-trial SBRT or hepatic resection on biology alone.
primary_concerns: The patient sits outside the guideline-endorsed population for any consolidation strategy; the de novo oligometastatic biology is intuitively appealing but no randomized signal supports off-trial consolidation.
If consolidation comes up in the family conversation, the consensus-aligned answer is 'on a trial, after systemic response, not as primary therapy.'
This pick is intentionally a non-intervention — the rank reflects that the consensus call is to NOT layer SBRT or hepatectomy onto the 1L systemic plan.

notes: Posture: anchored to the current consensus stack. NCCN Breast Cancer v2.2026 (Feb 27 2026 update) made two material moves since this case file was assembled — sacituzumab govitecan + pembrolizumab elevated to category 1 preferred for CPS >=10 1L mTNBC (ASCENT-04/KEYNOTE-D19), and sacituzumab govitecan monotherapy elevated to category 1 preferred for CPS <10 BRCA-WT 1L mTNBC (ASCENT-03). Neither displaces germline-BRCA-directed PARP-i, which remains category 1 preferred and can be started without waiting for the CPS read. I rank PARP-i first because the BRCA1 finding is the strongest single guideline anchor in the dossier and germline resolution is in-flight on the target_validation list; the CPS-anchored regimens follow as the second consensus stack, contingent on the CPS read. The carboplatin/gemcitabine chemo backbone is the contingency for CPS <10 with PARP-i declined. Pick 5 is the consensus AGAINST routine local consolidation (E2108, NRG-BR002) — included explicitly because this case file came in with curative-intent framing and a solitary liver lesion, and the consensus answer to 'should we resect or SBRT it?' is 'not off trial.' Off-guideline picks I would qualify or dissent on in round 2 if surfaced by other personas: CAPItello-290 capivasertib + paclitaxel (TNBC OS not met overall or in the AKT-altered subgroup; off-label in TNBC); ZEN-3694 + pembro + nab-paclitaxel (phase 1b dose-finding, no guideline endorsement); inavolisib + eribulin (off-label in TNBC, trial not yet recruiting); off-trial SBRT or hepatectomy of the liver lesion (E2108/NRG-BR002 against it). I will not veto these — they are not contraindicated, just outside the guideline-endorsed population for this patient — but I will mark them 'dissent on guideline_fit' in cross-critiques.

picks.intervention_label: Datopotamab deruxtecan + durvalumab on TROPION-Breast05 (NCT06103864)
picks.rationale: Upside: if the Dato-DXd + durvalumab arm beats the KEYNOTE-355 backbone we are otherwise going to give her, she gets a TROP2-ADC against the basal feature plus an ICI against the TIL-3+/TMB-14 phenotype, and she lands on the experimental arm of a registrational trial. She is the patient TROPION-Breast05 was built for. The downside is bounded because the control arm is the same regimen we would prescribe off-trial. The honest weakness is the readout is pending; I am buying expected value at PFS HR 0.57 from TROPION-Breast02 (pmid:41937088) translated forward to the CPS>=10 stratum.
primary_concerns: Gated on PD-L1 CPS >=10 by 22C3 (still pending); CPS<10 collapses this to the TROPION-Breast02 / TroFuse-011 axis instead.
ILD signal on the deruxtecan platform runs ~10% any-grade and ~2% G>=3 in the cumulative Dato-DXd dataset; counseling and active pulmonary surveillance are non-negotiable.
If she draws the control arm she gets standard-of-care, so the experimental-arm bet is the whole rationale; randomization risk is real.

picks.intervention_label: Olaparib 300 mg BID + durvalumab 1500 mg q4w as MEDIOLA-style maintenance after platinum + pembrolizumab induction
picks.rationale: MEDIOLA delivered DCR 80% and ORR 63% with median PFS 8.2 mo in germline-BRCA HER2-neg mBC on a single-arm n=34 (pmid:32771088), and TOPACIO replicated the chemo-free PARPi+ICI signal with 47% ORR in the BRCA-mut TNBC subset (pmid:31194225). The KEYLYNK-009 HRR-mut subgroup PFS HR ~0.65 (pmid:41405563) is the third independent hit on the same hypothesis. This patient is the canonical responder phenotype: BRCA1, TMB-14, TIL-3+, APOBEC-flavored (pmid:35168954). The thin part is single-arm data plus a negative overall KEYLYNK-009 readout; I am betting that the BRCA1+ICI-favorable subset is where the response actually lives.
primary_concerns: Off-label in 1L US TNBC; payer push-back is real and the regimen leans on subset/single-arm signals.

Sequencing question: induction with platinum + pembrolizumab first to establish response, then switch to olaparib + durvalumab maintenance — the strategy is mechanistically clean but the trial evidence for the exact switch is the negative-overall KEYLYNK-009.
Reversion-mutation surveillance baseline ctDNA needs to be drawn before olaparib starts (target_validation row brca-reversion-ctdna-baseline).

picks.intervention_label: SBRT to the solitary 1.5 cm hepatic lesion as consolidation on MSK SABR protocol (NCT05534438) after documented systemic response
picks.rationale: She has a single 1.5 cm liver lesion. This is the most consolidatable disease pattern she will ever present with, and she is 42 with a preference file that flags curative-intent framing. NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS was negative (HR ~1.31, pmid:33885704), which I am not hiding — that is the conservative anchor against routine consolidation. The risktaker case is that NRG-BR002 enrolled all subtypes and any-site oligomets; a BRCA1-mutated TNBC patient with a solitary liver lesion on systemic response is a biology-selected subset the trial was not powered to detect benefit in. The MSK protocol is the way to do this with a registered slot and a documented response gate, not on biology alone.
primary_concerns: NRG-BR002 phase IIR PFS readout was negative for consolidation; the biology-selection argument is post-hoc, not randomized.
Layered on top of (not instead of) picks 1-2; this is the curative-intent layer, not a systemic-therapy substitute.
Requires 12-week systemic response confirmation before SBRT, and a multidisciplinary IR/radiation-oncology slot at MSK (or an equivalent center) — logistics matter.

picks.intervention_label: ZEN-3694 (BET inhibitor) + pembrolizumab + nab-paclitaxel on NCT05422794
picks.rationale: MYC-amplified, basal-like, TIL-3+, TMB-14 — every axis this trial pre-specifies is lit up in her tumor. The CDK7/transcriptional-addiction preclinical for TNBC is Cell-quality (pmid:26406987), and the BET-inhibitor variant of that hypothesis is the closest active trial. Phase 1b means I am buying mechanistic fit, not phase 3 evidence; the honest read is no efficacy data yet and a real cumulative toxicity stack from BET-i layered on pembro + nab-paclitaxel. I rank it fourth because TROPION-Breast05's experimental arm covers most of the ICI + targeted-ADC bet with cleaner evidence; ZEN-3694 is the swing for the MYC-amp fences if the TROPION-Breast05 slot is not accessible.
primary_concerns: Phase 1b dose-finding; no published efficacy yet and the MYC-amplified expansion is hypothesis-generating, not powered.
BET-i + pembrolizumab + nab-paclitaxel layers hematologic, neuropathy, and irAE toxicity — manageable but cumulative; no veto in the preference file but counseling burden is high.
NCI sites only; if the patient is not near an enrolling center this pick demotes on logistics.

picks.intervention_label: Ceralasertib (AZD6738, ATR inhibitor) + olaparib on a successor VIOLETTE-style protocol
picks.rationale: BRCA1 + TP53 + PTEN loss is the cleanest replication-stress / DDR-addiction triad in the dossier. The preclinical synergy is unambiguous — complete regression of BRCA-mutant TNBC PDX with intermittent ceralasertib + continuous olaparib (pmid:35046096) — and the mechanism explains how to break PARPi resistance before it appears via RAD51-driven fork-protection rescue. The honest weakness is VIOLETTE was negative over olaparib alone (PFS HR ~0.81 in BRCA-mut, not significant); tolerability of intermittent ATRi at the active dose was the clinical headwind. The risktaker case: VIOLETTE used a dosing schedule the preclinical work suggested was suboptimal, and successor protocols are testing intensified intermittent dosing. Off-trial use is not defensible here; trial enrollment is the only honest path.
primary_concerns: VIOLETTE phase 2 was negative on the primary PFS endpoint; this is a 'bet on a better-designed successor' pick, not a 'bet on the existing trial' pick.
Hematologic toxicity of ATR + PARP combination is the rate-limiting clinical headwind; cumulative cytopenias compress dose intensity.
Need an active successor trial slot to execute on this; off-trial ceralasertib + olaparib is not on the table.

notes: Posture: efficacy lean 0.7, trial-prefer true, no toxicity vetoes, curative-intent framing in the free-text — this is the dossier I am supposed to swing for. TROPION-Breast05 at rank 1 is the highest expected-value play in the case: registrational design, mechanism aligned to the basal + TIL-rich + TMB-H axis, control arm bounded to standard-of-care. MEDIOLA-style maintenance at rank 2 is the chemo-free PARPi + ICI bet for the canonical responder phenotype she carries; evidence is single-arm + subset, which is exactly the trade-off this seat tolerates. SBRT consolidation at rank 3 is the curative-intent layer that the conservative seat will undersell — I am acknowledging the negative NRG-BR002 readout and arguing biology selection through the MSK trial slot. ZEN-3694 at rank 4 is the MYC-amp swing on a phase 1b; I rank it below TROPION-Breast05 only because the ICI + chemo bet is covered there with stronger evidence. Ceralasertib + olaparib at rank 5 is the DDR-addiction bet; honest about the VIOLETTE negative and only viable through a successor trial. Deliberate omissions: olaparib monotherapy (covered by the conservative and critic seats, lower expected-value than the combination strategies for this phenotype); capivasertib + paclitaxel (CAPItello-290 OS negative in the AKT-altered subgroup, even my appetite has a floor); inavolisib + eribulin (PIK3CA hotspot ngs_pending, trial not yet recruiting, eribulin backbone requires taxane pretreatment); the somatic-talazoparib Stanford trial (NCT03990896) sits in the dossier as the contingency if BRCA1 resolves to somatic-only — I would surface it in cross-critiques rather than rank it here. CPS-gating drives the rank shuffle if 22C3 returns <10: TROPION-Breast02 (NCT05374512, PFS HR 0.57) or TroFuse-011 (NCT06841354) take rank 1, and the MEDIOLA maintenance bet moves up.
